Editor.ResyncHint: Re-create any missing granted effects on their current targets (late joiners, roster changes, hand-deleted effects)
Editor.PlaceHint: Put currency into a chest or an NPC for the party to find
Editor.NoSections: No sections yet. Upgrades show as one flat list until you add some.
Editor.NoUpgrades: No upgrades yet — create your first one.
Editor.ClearHint: Sweep the log. Balances and owned upgrades are not read from it and do not change.
Editor.RemoveLine: Remove this line from the log
Editor.Title: Upgrades — GM Console

UpgradeEditor.Name: Name
UpgradeEditor.FlavorEg: Worn smooth by years of use.
UpgradeEditor.ComesAfterHint: Tick anything that must be owned before this can be bought. It stays visible but locked until then, and the two are shown as linked.
UpgradeEditor.CannotTakeWithHint: Tick anything the party must choose between. Buying either one rules out the other — refunding it opens the choice again. Ticking here says the same thing as ticking this upgrade over there, so it only needs doing once.
UpgradeEditor.Repeatable: Can be bought more than once
UpgradeEditor.BuyerHint: Resolved when it is bought: a player's assigned character, or — if a GM buys it — whoever the GM picks. Combine with “can be bought more than once” for something each character acquires separately, like a tangible item.
UpgradeEditor.NoTargetWarn: Pick a character, or the effect will have nowhere to land.
UpgradeEditor.BuilderUnsupported: The bonus builder ships presets for dnd5e and PF2e. In {system} you can still add custom targets below, or link an existing effect instead.
UpgradeEditor.PresetTitle: Choose what this bonus applies to
UpgradeEditor.BonusTypeTitle: PF2e counts only the highest bonus of each type
UpgradeEditor.Pf2eDice: Enter a flat number like 1, or dice like 1d6. Extra dice have no bonus type, so that dropdown disappears when you type dice.
UpgradeEditor.Pf2eWhyType: Why the type matters: PF2e adds only the largest bonus of each type. Two item bonuses to AC do not become +2 — the bigger one simply wins.
UpgradeEditor.Pf2eUntyped: If you only want it to work and do not care about the maths, pick Untyped.
UpgradeEditor.Dnd5eFormula: Values are dnd5e roll formulas, and they should carry a sign: +2 for a flat bonus, +1d8[cold] for typed dice — that is how “every weapon swing deals an extra 1d8 cold” is written. The sign is added for you if you leave it off; it matters because two upgrades touching the same bonus are joined end to end, and +2+3 works where 23 does not. Ability scores and darkvision are plain numbers, so those take 2 and 60.
UpgradeEditor.DragEffect: Drag an Effect or Item here
UpgradeEditor.DragEffectHint: from a character sheet, the Items sidebar, or a compendium
UpgradeEditor.DragItemHint: from a character sheet — the upgrade lands on that very item
UpgradeEditor.ItemUnresolved: The chosen item no longer exists. Drop a new one here.
UpgradeEditor.ItemUnowned: Nobody carries this item any more, so its effect reaches no one until someone picks it up.
UpgradeEditor.ItemTargetHint: The effect travels with the item and applies to whoever has it equipped — attuned or invested where the system asks for it. A stashed item grants nothing.
UpgradeEditor.UuidEg: filled in by dragging, or paste one
UpgradeEditor.UuidUnresolved: That UUID does not resolve to a document in this world.
UpgradeEditor.ShowInEffectsBar: Show it in the effects bar
UpgradeEditor.KeepSecret: Keep what it does secret until it is owned
UpgradeEditor.Nominate: Have them nominate something when they buy this
UpgradeEditor.Question: Question
UpgradeEditor.GuidanceEg: Drag a spell from your spellbook.
UpgradeEditor.ChoiceHint: A window opens before the cost is paid; cancelling it buys nothing. What they pick names the granted item — “Temporary Scroll (Fireball)” — and is linked inside its description. Their answer is remembered, so re-syncing rebuilds the same personalised grant.

Dnd5e.spell_damage_all: All spell damage (incl. saving throw spells)
Dnd5e.item_magic: Magical bonus (attack and damage; AC on armor)
Dnd5e.item_damage: Extra damage dealt by this item

Pf2e.rune_potency: Potency rune (attack, or AC on armor)

BonusType.circumstance: Circumstance — from where you are or what you did
BonusType.circumstanceHint: Terrain, cover, a lit beacon, a clever plan. The usual choice for something the world provides.
BonusType.item: Item — from gear, a rune, an installed upgrade
BonusType.itemHint: Will not stack with a magic weapon or armour giving the same kind of bonus — the larger one wins.
BonusType.status: Status — from a spell, condition or blessing
BonusType.statusHint: Will not stack with spell buffs like Bless that grant the same kind of bonus.
BonusType.untypedHint: Nothing suppresses it. Use it when you just want the bonus to apply, at the cost of breaking PF2e's stacking maths.
BonusType.proficiencyHint: Reserved for training rank. Almost never what an upgrade should grant.
BonusType.abilityHint: Reserved for an attribute modifier. Almost never what an upgrade should grant.

Setting.PlayersCanOpen: Players can open the window freely
Setting.AutoDeposit: Credit currency automatically when picked up

SettingHint.ActionVerb: The label on the purchase button. E.g. “Buy”, “Request”, “Claim”.
SettingHint.CurrencyIcon: A Font Awesome class (e.g. “fa-solid fa-seedling”) or a path to an image in your Foundry data folder.
SettingHint.CurrencyItem: An Item representing one unit, so the currency can be looted from a chest or a body.
SettingHint.CurrencyName: The resource that is spent. E.g. “Marks”.
SettingHint.HostActor: Double-clicking this actor's token opens the window, so the party has somewhere to go.
SettingHint.HostImg: Path to an image in your Foundry data folder. Leave empty for a default icon.
SettingHint.HostName: The NPC or place presenting the upgrades. E.g. “The Quartermaster”.
SettingHint.PartyActor: The Group (dnd5e) or Party (PF2e) actor whose members count as “the party” for party-wide upgrades. Strongly recommended: without it the module falls back to every player-owned character, which in a world full of loot, summon and wildshape actors is rarely what you want.
SettingHint.PlayersCanOpen: If disabled, players only see it when the GM shows it to them.
SettingHint.RequireApproval: If enabled, player purchase requests must be approved by the GM before the cost is deducted.
SettingHint.Theme: Colour and texture of the player-facing window.
SettingHint.WindowTitle: Shown in the window title bar. E.g. “The Exchange”.

PartyNote.Fallback: No party actor is configured in module settings, so this falls back to all {count} player-owned character(s) — worth setting properly before using party-wide upgrades.

GrantNote.ActiveEffect: Granted as an Active Effect, so it sits on the Effects tab
GrantNote.QuietFeature: Granted as a quiet, permanent feature on the sheet
GrantNote.OnItem: Placed on the item itself, applying to whoever has it equipped
GrantNote.Sentence: {how}; removing or refunding the upgrade deletes it again.
GrantNote.AlreadyOwned: This upgrade is already owned — saving re-applies it to its targets.

Dialog.DeleteUpgradeOwned: It is currently owned — its effect will also be removed from every character that has it.
Dialog.RefundBody: Refund {name} — {price} back, and its effect removed from {who}?
Dialog.RefundRemaining: {count} other acquisition(s) of this upgrade are left untouched.
Dialog.DeleteSectionKeeps: Its {count} upgrade(s) are kept — they simply become uncategorised.
Dialog.ClearHistoryBody: The history is a record of what happened — it is not what the balances or the owned upgrades are read from. Clearing it moves no {currency}, and un-buys nothing.
Dialog.EditReasonNote: The amount stays as it is — a ledger that can be made to disagree with the balance it describes is worse than none.
Dialog.RemoveResourceNote: Its balance is discarded, and any upgrade priced in it stops costing it.

Notify.PickAnItem: Upgrades: pick an item for an item upgrade.

Notify.ItemLinkUnsupported: Upgrades: “{name}” links a document an item cannot carry — build the effect instead, or link an Active Effect.

Notify.RuneWrongItemType: Upgrades: “{item}” cannot take “{label}” — wrong kind of item.

Notify.RuneNotBetter: Upgrades: “{item}” already has a rune at least that strong — nothing was added.
Notify.RuneAbp: Upgrades: this world uses Automatic Bonus Progression, which suppresses rune values — the rune was recorded but will not apply.
Notify.RuneNeedsPotency: Upgrades: “{item}” carries more property runes than its potency has slots for; the extra stays dormant until the potency rises.
Notify.RuneChangedByHand: Upgrades: a rune on “{item}” was changed by hand after this purchase, so that value was left as it is.
Notify.ItemRowsDropped: Upgrades: bonus rows that only work on an item were removed — this upgrade no longer targets one.
Notify.Migrated: Upgrade Board: your existing board came across from the older “Upgrades” module ({count} upgrades). You can safely disable that one now.
